liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain and Snow** (2 reviews): The crowd can be heard singing along with the band on the chorus of the opener; Audience energy during the opener is striking on the recording [27][28]
- **Baby What You Want Me to Do?** (1 review): Brent's vocal on this song showcases strong blues playing [32]
- **Jam** (1 review): The jam before drums features xylophones and recalls the experiments of 1986 [32]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Reviewer says Jerry fades after space and sounds off; the closer rushes like a horse nearing the barn [29]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Supplication jam as sweet, and also praises Tennessee Jed [31]

## The recordings

- **gd85-03-29.aud.barbella.10493.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 133 min; rated 4/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1985-03-29.165162.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 138 min [2]
- **gd1985-03-29.149308.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 137 min [6]
- **gd1985-03-29.141208.unknown.Bryant.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 136 min [12]

## Around the show

- A front-row woman got past security onto the stage, touched Brent's head, and danced before Jerry until escorted off [26]
- Jerry reacted to the stage-crasher by saying the line about women being smarter, that's right [26]
- Bob opened the second set asking for a bumper sticker reading that Phil loves New York [30]
- A woman jumped on stage during this song, as the reviewer, who attended, recalls [30]
- Matt Kelly sits in on Ain't Superstitious and the Bottom, according to this reviewer [34]
- Seating was general admission on this tour; a blind man in front of reviewer was ecstatic through set one [35]
- Mickey hit Matthew Kelly with multiple drum sticks [2]
- A woman jumped on stage and danced between Bob and Jerry briefly before security escorted her off [2]
- Reviewer ranks this second among spring 1985 shows, behind the March 31 show [27]
- Reviewer finds the first set strong enough that the show could have been the year's best until drums [29]
- Reviewer thinks the band played better the first night and that its sound has more impact; also suggests the 2/20/85 audience tape [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-03-29.aud.barbella.10493.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Audience recording went microphone to cassette to DAT to CDR, via Raul, seeded to etree by Steve Barbella [1]
- **gd1985-03-29.165162.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 shotguns > Sony D5M [2]. Also: Source from Stephen Thomas's master cassettes, coordinated by Charlie Miller; Oade's Schoeps CMC4 MK source supplies crowd, a Minglewood start, and a Drums patch [2]
- **gd1985-03-29.149308.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [6]
- **gd1985-03-29.141208.unknown.Bryant.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Robert Bryant recording: unknown mics > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M); Charlie Miller DSD [12]. Also: File set is 16 bit, converted from 24 bit using MusicConverter with sox [12]
